free_tier.stated: No episode caps, no storage limits, no upcharging as your show grows. Unlimited hosting, included in every plan.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: The hosting page publishes no per-episode file-size cap. The recording product's limits are a separate product and are not a hosting cap.

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: The hosting page states no episode retention period; the recording product's separate limit is not a hosting term.

egress.terms: Not metered in any published doc; hosting and publishing show 'Unlimited' in the plan comparison.

tooling: No public upload API found; dashboard upload only. RSS out is standard.
chaining: 5 shows per free account x unlimited episodes x unpublished per-file cap. Multiple accounts = 5 shows each.
limits_note: Per-episode file size is NOT published. This is the risk. Zencastr also sells a recording product whose free tier is separately capped at '2 hours of audio and video recording per month' with 'Recording masters storage of up to 31 days' (2023 change), which is easy to confuse with hosting; hosting is the uncapped part, recording masters are not.

identity_cost.detail: sign-up is a Create Account form with first name, last name, username, email and password; no card or phone field is shown.

reliability_note: No independent confirmation of transcode behaviour and no live enclosure probe possible without an account. Trust level is 'vendor says unlimited' with no number to check, which per the brief's own rules caps this at medium. Their 2023 free-plan reduction shows the free tier is a moving target.
